A college student steps up to confront Joshua Haymes and laughs as she tells him illegal immigrants are “making this country a good country.”

Then he says one thing that wipes the smile off her face, leaving her dead silent with zero pushback.

HAYMES: “They broke the law. The punishment for breaking that particular law is deportation. Therefore, we should deport all the people who broke that law. That’s just logic.”

STUDENT: “I don’t think so. [...] They came here and they’re making this country a good country.”

HAYMES: “I would say that merely by the fact that the first act they did was break the law, they are not making the country a better country. They are filling the country with criminals because they themselves are criminals. [...] They are criminals, right?”

STUDENT: “Well, they came here and they overstayed, and then the law does say that.”

HAYMES: “Correct. [...] And so what do we do with criminals in a just society?”

STUDENT: “Punish them.”

HAYMES: “We punish them. So, it makes sense. I mean, it sounds like we agree.”

Clutching her backpack straps, she giggles: “But no.”

HAYMES: “But we shouldn’t punish the criminals?”

STUDENT: “Okay, but they’re helping economically and everything.”

HAYMES: “So if someone is beating their wife, but they’re helping economically, I would say we should still throw them in prison. You would agree?”

STUDENT: “That is not the same thing, though.”

HAYMES: “Helping the economy doesn’t get you off scot-free from breaking other laws. You would agree with that, right?”

STUDENT: “Yeah.”

Then Haymes tells her the real reason she’s defending them.

HAYMES: “It seems like you have an irrational position, and you know it’s irrational, but you have a bias because it’s your people. And so you want what’s best for your people, and I get that. But I am American, and I want what’s best for my people.”

“And it just so happens that allowing illegal immigrants into the country to just stay here, overstay their visas, and remain here illegally, is bad for my people and my country.”

This time, she didn’t giggle.

ADDED CONTEXT: Illegal immigration costs U.S. taxpayers a net $150,700,000,000 a year, even after subtracting the taxes illegal immigrants pay, according to a FAIR estimate cited by the House Budget Committee.
